1.why: All screens show a clean static layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions use solid blue buttons and section headings stand out, though the always-visible activity log competes somewhat for attention.

3.why: Each step presents a single clear form and labeled button so the next required action is easy to locate.

4.why: The flow requires the user to remember and carry forward a long recovery token plus a separate MFA code across multiple distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Aside from the pre-filled demo token, the interface provides no saved or familiar personal items for the user to recognize.

7.why: Labels and instructional sentences are generally short and plainly worded, although security notices add extra length.

8.why: No error messages or validation failures are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: Demo screens explicitly display the test token and six-digit code to type, and password rules are listed as concrete examples.

10.why: The only authentication path offered is password reset; no alternative choices such as code or face login are presented.

11.why: Each step limits the user to one or two inputs and a single primary button, avoiding simultaneous choice overload.

12.why: Green success banners and the final “Recovery complete” screen clearly state the outcome of each major action.

13.why: Contextual info banners appear on most steps, yet dedicated help links or expandable short tips for new actions are absent.

14.why: A “Start over” button is available early and the user can simply re-enter data on later forms if a mistake is made.

15.why: Every screen re-uses the same header, card layout, button style, and safety footer, keeping the design consistent.
